hero.subtitle: About Me
hero.p1: Hello! I am a passionate canine behaviorist, dedicated to strengthening the unique bond between every dog and their human.
hero.p2: My approach goes far beyond simply "teaching commands". My goal is to give you the keys to understand your companion: their needs, emotions, and body language.
hero.p3: Moving away from outdated coercive methods, I advocate for 100% positive and compassionate training, based on the latest scientific advances in ethology.

values.title: My Training Philosophy
values.subtitle: Every dog is an individual. There is no "magic formula", but constant adaptation guided by three core pillars.
values.val1Desc: No violence, physical or psychological. We work with the dog's motivation (toys, treats, praise) to create joyful cooperation.
values.val2Desc: I continuously educate myself on new discoveries in canine ethology to offer you modern, ethical, and effective solutions.
values.val3Desc: Your life, your environment, and your dog are unique. I adapt each exercise so that it is achievable and relevant in your daily life.

hero.title: A Scientific & Compassionate Approach
hero.subtitle: Dog training has evolved. Forget dominance and force. My methodology is based on ethology and the laws of learning for lasting results.

philosophy.p1: Far from being a "permissive" method, compassionate training is a rigorous approach that respects the physical and emotional integrity of the dog. We do not seek to submit the animal, but to obtain its
philosophy.p2: In concrete terms, we reinforce good behaviors (rewards, games, praise) so that they are repeated, and we manage the environment to avoid mistakes, without ever using fear or pain.
philosophy.frameDesc: Compassion does not mean laxity. I work with a clear and coherent framework. Rules and boundaries are essential for your dog to feel secure. My role is to help you set this structuring framework, but always in a fair and explainable way to the dog.
philosophy.p3: My practice is based on factual data from ethology (the study of behavior) and behavioral psychology.
philosophy.point1Desc: The dog learns through the consequences of its actions. A pleasant consequence reinforces the behavior.
philosophy.point2Desc: Every dog has its own motivations, fears, and tolerance thresholds. No "magic recipe", but a tailor-made approach.
philosophy.point3Desc: Your dog is a being endowed with exceptional cognitive abilities. Rather than using coercion or coercive tools, we stimulate its intelligence. It is its capacity to think and understand that generates lasting progress.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.subtitle: Understand my profession, my methods, and how the sessions work.

questions.question: What is a dog trainer and what do they do?
questions.answer: A dog trainer is a specialist in the Human-Dog relationship. My role is not simply to "train" your animal, but to provide you with the tools to understand and communicate clearly with them. This helps establish healthy living rules, solve everyday problems (potty training, destruction, loneliness), and guarantee the safety and well-being of everyone.

questions.question: What can this bring me?
questions.answer: Beyond pure obedience, it brings you peace of mind. You will learn to decode your dog's signals, prevent conflicts, and strengthen your bond. It's an investment to build a harmonious relationship that will last 10 or 15 years.

questions.question: Who is this for?
questions.answer: Everyone! Puppy owners who want to start on the right foot, families experiencing difficulties with an adult dog, or simply enthusiasts who want to deepen their bond. There are no "bad owners", only pairs that need adjustments.

questions.question: When should I call a dog trainer?
questions.answer: Prevention is ideal: as soon as the puppy arrives or even before adoption. However, you should consult as soon as a problematic behavior appears (aggression, fear, excessive barking). Do not wait for the situation to escalate; it is always easier to prevent than to cure.

questions.question: Is it still possible to change my dog's behavior (despite their age/past)?
questions.answer: YES, absolutely. A dog's brain remains plastic throughout its life. Whether they are 5, 10 years old, or have a heavy past (shelter, abuse), we can always modify behaviors and soothe emotions. It sometimes requires more patience than with a puppy, but progress is always possible.

questions.question: What methods do you use?
questions.answer: I work exclusively with positive and compassionate methods, based on behavioral sciences (ethology). We use the dog's motivation (toys, rewards) to reinforce good behaviors. I refuse any coercive tools (choke collars, shock collars) or physical/psychological violence.

questions.question: Where do the sessions take place?
questions.answer: The Behavioral Assessment (1st session) must take place at your home to observe the dog in its real environment. Follow-up sessions can then take place at home or outdoors (park, city, forest) depending on the issues to be addressed (loose leash walking, recall, socialization).

questions.question: How do I request a first session?
questions.answer: You can contact me via the website form or by phone. Together we will arrange an appointment for a Behavioral Assessment (duration 1.5 to 2 hours). This is the essential step for me to analyze the situation and offer you a customized training plan.

questions.question: Do you offer payment plans?
questions.answer: Yes. The behavioral assessment must be paid on the day of the session. However, for training or rehabilitation packages, you have the option to pay in 2 installments free of charge to spread the cost.
